purpose: Focused, bounded numerical audit of the JP-JEPA Mini CPU-vs-GPU jet_embedding discrepancy first surfaced in dual_canary_report.json (2026-08-25). No new JP-JEPA production, no SPA-Net training performed.

runtime_settings_verified_by_code_audit.dtype: float32 throughout (no .half()/.double() cast anywhere; checkpoint itself is fp32)
runtime_settings_verified_by_code_audit.autocast: NOT used anywhere in extract_shard.py or layer_hook_localization.py
runtime_settings_verified_by_code_audit.explicit_tf32_control: NOT set anywhere (no torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32, no torch.set_float32_matmul_precision call) -- PyTorch defaults apply (matmul TF32 disabled by default since torch 1.12; CPU is unaffected by TF32 regardless)
runtime_settings_verified_by_code_audit.attention_backend: nn.MultiheadAttention called with default need_weights=True in every Block.forward (both jpjepa_src/particle_transformer.py and the vendored ParT weaver_core_part/ParticleTransformer.py) because attn_matrix is captured and returned as part of all_outputs -- this forces PyTorch's explicit reference math attention path on BOTH CPU and GPU (fused flash/mem-efficient SDPA kernels are only selected by PyTorch when need_weights=False), ruling out 'different fused attention kernel on GPU' as an explanation
runtime_settings_verified_by_code_audit.deterministic_algorithms: torch.use_deterministic_algorithms() NOT called anywhere -- PyTorch defaults apply

cpu_vs_gpu_final_jet_embedding.cpu_run: bs=512, this project's CPU tiny-test receipt (2026-08-25), torch 2.8.0+cpu
cpu_vs_gpu_final_jet_embedding.gpu_run: bs=256, EAF A100 80GB PCIe MIG 4g.40gb, torch 2.8.0+cu128, run1 (independently cross-checked against run2, bitwise identical to run1)
cpu_vs_gpu_final_jet_embedding.independently_reproduced_this_session: yes -- recomputed directly from the raw per-jet EMBEDDINGS/jpjepa_mini arrays in cpu_reference/train_0000_cpu_dual.h5 and canary_eaf/run1/train_0000.h5, not merely re-reading dual_canary_report.json's own aggregate numbers. Result matches dual_canary_report.json exactly.
cpu_vs_gpu_final_jet_embedding.outlier_structure: no small set of pathological jets dominates -- rel_l2 distribution is smooth (median 0.00074, p99 0.00203, max 0.00469, only ~6x median at the single worst jet out of 12089); correlation of rel_l2 with jet_pt=0.10, with n_constituents=-0.09, with embedding norm=-0.07 (all weak) -- consistent with generic float32 backend noise, not a specific pathological input regime (e.g. extreme multiplicity or d0/dz-saturated tracks)
cpu_vs_gpu_final_jet_embedding.per_dimension_structure: divergence is spread across most of the 128 output dims (median fraction of squared-diff-energy carried by the single worst dim = 0.114, i.e. no dim dominates); dim 123 is the most affected on average (mean_abs_diff=0.00539, ~4x the per-dim median of 0.00132), dims 60/78/45 also mildly elevated (~2.5-3x median) -- a mild, not extreme, concentration

gpu_run_to_run_determinism.comparison: GPU run1 (bs=256) vs GPU run2 (bs=256), same EAF A100 MIG slice
gpu_run_to_run_determinism.verdict: bitwise identical -- GPU is internally deterministic for this fixed shape/batch-size/hardware combination even without torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

part_full_part_for_comparison.source: eaf_gpu_validation_20260825/CPU_GPU_COMPARISON.txt (ParT_full.pt, same architecture hyperparameters as JP-JEPA Mini: embed_dims=[128,512,128], num_heads=8, num_layers=8, num_cls_layers=2, verified via canonical_part_jet_encoder.py docstring)
part_full_part_for_comparison.note: ParT and JP-JEPA Mini share identical layer/head/embed-dim hyperparameters and are BOTH official, frozen, non-fine-tuned JetClass-pretrained checkpoints applied out-of-domain to the same AK4 jets with the same attention-kernel path forced (need_weights=True) -- yet JP-JEPA's CPU/GPU divergence is systematically larger: ~17.5x max_abs, ~150x mean_abs, ~4.8x max_rel_l2, ~13x median_rel_l2. Domain shift and attention-kernel selection are therefore ruled out as differentiators (both models face identical exposure to both); the residual difference is attributed to checkpoint-specific numerical conditioning (different pretraining objective -- JEPA self-supervised vs ParT's supervised JetClass classification -- yields different weight-magnitude/activation statistics), not to any difference in this project's extraction code, which is identical in structure for both models.

cpu_layer_by_layer_magnitude_profile.note: GPU-side layer-by-layer capture (gpu_layers.npz) could NOT be produced in this session -- no GPU device was reachable (see execution_environment_limitations below). The existing CPU-only capture (cpu_layers.npz, 200 fixed jets, prior session) was independently reproduced bit-for-bit in this session (see batch_size_invariance.reproduction_of_frozen_artifact) and is analyzed here for activation-magnitude structure as the best available evidence of WHERE in the depth of the network divergence is architecturally most likely to be amplified, absent a literal GPU-side counterpart.
cpu_layer_by_layer_magnitude_profile.finding: activation magnitude (mean_abs) grows through main blocks 0-3 (peaking near layer 3, ~2.6x layer 0), decays through layers 4-7, then jumps sharply at the two class-attention blocks: layer_08 mean_abs is 2.97x layer_07, and layer_09 (=jet_embedding, the frozen extraction point) mean_abs is a further 1.90x layer_08, with by far the largest max_abs (24.9, vs <10 for every main block) and largest std (2.68) of any captured layer. This is consistent with the class-attention mechanism's full-sequence, softmax-weighted aggregation over a 128-slot sequence that is >80% zero-padding for typical AK4 jets (mean 17.8 real constituents, FEATURE_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX.md section 5) being the most numerically sensitive stage of the network: small per-constituent logit perturbations among the few real (non-padded) constituents can shift softmax attention weights non-negligibly when so few tokens compete for weight, and this stage sits last -- with no subsequent block to average the effect back down. This is the leading architectural hypothesis for where CPU/GPU divergence is most likely amplified, though it is inferred from CPU-only dynamic-range structure, not a direct CPU-vs-GPU layer diff.

reproduction_of_frozen_artifact.description: Re-ran the exact frozen extract_shard.py code (sha256-verified) against the exact frozen checkpoint/manifest (sha256-verified) on the same 200 fixed jets (identity-verified against cpu_layers.npz's native_hdf5_row_index/jet_slot), batch_size=200 single batch, in a fresh CPU-only venv (torch 2.8.0+cpu) this session.

cpu_bs200_vs_bs1_fully_serial.note: the ONE nonzero batch-size effect found in this audit: fully-serial (bs=1) inference differs from batched (bs=64 or bs=200) inference by up to 1.34e-5 (absolute), presumably due to different BLAS call paths for batched vs single-sample matmul. This is ~4500x SMALLER than the CPU-vs-GPU max_abs_diff (0.0597), so it does not explain the CPU/GPU gap -- it is cited here as a genuine, freshly-measured upper bound on how large a pure batch-size effect can possibly be on this architecture, which supports (rather than undermines) the prior finding that batch size is not the cause of the CPU/GPU discrepancy.

batch_size_invariance.prior_evidence_context: This task's brief states CPU@512 == CPU@256 and CPU@256 vs GPU@256 reproduces the discrepancy, established in an earlier session not captured in this checkpoint package's docs. This session's own bs=200-vs-bs=64 CPU-only bitwise-identical result, plus the bs=1 upper bound above, is consistent with and reinforces that conclusion using freshly-executed evidence.

signal_vs_noise_downstream_impact_argume.conclusion: Even the single worst CPU/GPU-divergent jet out of 12089 (absolute L2 diff 0.152) is ~22x smaller than the closest 1st-percentile nearest-neighbor jet-to-jet distance (3.33) within the SAME process (QCD), and ~6x smaller than the smallest between-process mean-embedding separation (0.91, QCD vs global mean). The mean CPU/GPU noise (0.025) is ~36x smaller than that same process separation and ~230x smaller than the typical nearest-neighbor jet distance (5.8). CPU/GPU backend noise at this scale cannot plausibly cause two jets, or two processes, to become indistinguishable in the frozen 128-d representation that SPA-Net will consume as an input feature.
